Bug_Details:
A method should not have the same name as its containing class.
This would be confusing as it would look like a constructor.
Examples:
public class MyClass {

    public MyClass() {}         // this is OK because it is a constructor

    public void MyClass() {}    // this is bad because it is a method
}
Bug_Explanation: A method with the same name as its containing class was created, which is confusing as it looks like a constructor.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the testShowBug method is called in the MyClassTest class. This method in turn calls the showBug method in the MyClass class, which further calls the method with the same name as the class. This is not allowed and should cause a compilation error.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results show that the test passed successfully without any errors. This indicates that the method with the same name as the enclosing class did not cause any issues during the execution of the test. Therefore, the test results do not confirm the presence of the described bug in the Java code.
